[standards/governance/ai/STD-GOV-AI-005-ai-portfolio-hygiene.md#purpose-statement]

### Purpose Statement

This standard prevents capability sprawl and maintains a healthy, reusable, low-duplication enterprise AI agent portfolio. It defines the registry data required to govern the portfolio, the process for duplicate and overlap control, the conditions that trigger rationalization review, and the rules governing capability consolidation and retirement.
page_texts.5:
[standards/governance/ai/STD-GOV-AI-005-ai-portfolio-hygiene.md#scope]

### Scope

This standard applies to all enterprise AI agents at Proposed, Pilot, and Production lifecycle states. It applies to both AI Agents (Configured) and Custom AI Agents.
page_texts.6:
[standards/governance/ai/STD-GOV-AI-005-ai-portfolio-hygiene.md#compliance-level]

### Compliance Level

Mandatory. No capability may enter Pilot state without a registry entry. No capability may remain in Production state without current registry data.
page_texts.7:
[standards/governance/ai/STD-GOV-AI-005-ai-portfolio-hygiene.md#business-rationale]

### Business Rationale

Federated delivery models produce multiple teams building independently toward overlapping intents. Without active portfolio hygiene, the portfolio accumulates redundant capabilities that compete for the same user population, create inconsistent outputs from semantically identical intents, increase maintenance burden, and become ungovernable. Portfolio hygiene is not a cleanup activity — it is an ongoing governance discipline.

page_texts.9:
[standards/governance/ai/STD-GOV-AI-005-ai-portfolio-hygiene.md#mandatory-requirements]

### Mandatory Requirements

**Portfolio Registry Data Requirements:**

The capability registry must maintain the following fields for every registered capability:

1. Capability domain — the enterprise domain this capability serves
2. Agent owner — the named individual accountable for quality, currency, and compliance of this capability
3. Lifecycle state — the current state from the lifecycle model defined in STD-TEC-AI-001
4. Active intents — the enumerated list of in-scope intents from the capability contract
5. Last validation date — the date quality rubric evaluation was most recently completed
6. Quality trend status — a current-period assessment of whether quality metrics are stable, improving, or declining
7. Usage level — a usage volume indicator for the current reporting period per STD-TEC-AI-006
8. Duplicate risk indicator — an assessment of whether high-overlap capabilities exist in the registry

**Duplicate and Overlap Controls:**

- New capability proposals must include an overlap analysis against all existing registered capabilities before approval to enter Pilot state
- Capabilities identified as having high overlap must be assessed for merge, split, or deprecation before the new proposal proceeds
- Duplicate intent patterns — where two or more capabilities respond to semantically equivalent intents — require a consolidation plan before either may remain in or enter Production state

**Rationalization Triggers:**

A rationalization review is triggered when any one of the following conditions is met:

1. High overlap with an existing registered capability is confirmed by the overlap analysis
2. Usage volume is below the defined minimum threshold for the relevant reporting period, as defined in the domain's portfolio governance documentation
3. Defect rate or rework rate exceeds the capability's quality rubric thresholds for two consecutive review cycles
4. No active owner is assigned — the capability has no named accountable individual
5. Validation date is stale — the last quality rubric evaluation is older than the review cadence defined in the domain's portfolio governance documentation

**Consolidation and Retirement Rules:**

- Consolidation of two or more capabilities requires a migration plan and a user communication plan before consolidation is executed
- Retirement of a capability requires a successor mapping — identifying what replaces the capability for affected users — or an explicit gap acceptance recorded in the architecture record
- Retired capabilities must remain discoverable in archive records; they must not be deleted from the registry

**Portfolio Review Cadence:**

- Monthly domain hygiene review: validate registry data currency, review rationalization triggers, track open consolidation plans
- Quarterly enterprise consolidation review: identify patterns of portfolio duplication across domains; review capabilities that have been in a rationalization-triggered state without a resolution plan
- Annual domain topology reassessment: evaluate whether the domain segmentation of the portfolio remains aligned with the enterprise AI taxonomy (per GUID-TEC-AI-001)
page_texts.10:
[standards/governance/ai/STD-GOV-AI-005-ai-portfolio-hygiene.md#recommended-practices]

### Recommended Practices

- Run overlap analysis against the registry before the build phase begins, not at the Pilot promotion gate — discovering high overlap after significant build investment is costly
- Assign backup owners at registration time to prevent ownerless-capability rationalization triggers when primary owners change roles
page_texts.11:
[standards/governance/ai/STD-GOV-AI-005-ai-portfolio-hygiene.md#prohibited-practices]

### Prohibited Practices

- Capabilities that have not been registered in the portfolio registry must not be promoted to Pilot state
- Capabilities confirmed as high-overlap with an existing registered capability must not be promoted to Production state without a recorded consolidation plan or explicit architectural justification
page_texts.12:
[standards/governance/ai/STD-GOV-AI-005-ai-portfolio-hygiene.md#exceptions-process]

### Exceptions Process

1. Requests to proceed with a high-overlap capability without consolidation require Enterprise Copilot Architecture Board approval and a documented rationale for why the capabilities are not substitutable
2. Exception records are retained in the capability registry as a component of the capability's record

---
page_texts.15:
[standards/governance/ai/STD-GOV-AI-005-ai-portfolio-hygiene.md#registry-currency-requirements]

#### Registry Currency Requirements

- Registry data must be updated within five business days of any change to the fields specified in the portfolio registry data requirements
- Stale registry data — any required field not updated within one review cycle without a recorded reason — constitutes non-compliance
page_texts.16:
[standards/governance/ai/STD-GOV-AI-005-ai-portfolio-hygiene.md#overlap-analysis-method]

#### Overlap Analysis Method

- Overlap analysis must compare the proposed capability's in-scope intents against the active intents of all existing registered capabilities at the same lifecycle state or higher
- Overlap is assessed at the intent level, not at the capability name level; two capabilities with different names may have overlapping intents
page_texts.17:
[standards/governance/ai/STD-GOV-AI-005-ai-portfolio-hygiene.md#archive-record-requirements]

#### Archive Record Requirements

- Retired capability records must include the retirement date, the successor capability or gap acceptance record, and the date on which the owner confirmed the migration was complete

---
page_texts.20:
[standards/governance/ai/STD-GOV-AI-005-ai-portfolio-hygiene.md#phase-1-portfolio-registry-establishment]

#### Phase 1: Portfolio Registry Establishment

1. Register all capabilities in Proposed, Pilot, or Production state in the portfolio registry with all required fields
2. Run an initial overlap analysis across all registered capabilities to identify existing high-overlap pairs
3. Produce a rationalization status for each existing high-overlap pair — merge, split, or justified co-existence
page_texts.21:
[standards/governance/ai/STD-GOV-AI-005-ai-portfolio-hygiene.md#phase-2-new-capability-registration]

#### Phase 2: New Capability Registration

1. Before any new capability enters Pilot state: run overlap analysis, record results in the registry, and confirm no unresolved high-overlap condition exists
2. Register the capability with all required fields, including the agent owner, lifecycle state, and active intents
page_texts.22:
[standards/governance/ai/STD-GOV-AI-005-ai-portfolio-hygiene.md#phase-3-ongoing-portfolio-governance]

#### Phase 3: Ongoing Portfolio Governance

1. Conduct monthly domain hygiene review: validate registry data currency, review rationalization triggers, track open consolidation plans
2. Conduct quarterly enterprise consolidation review: identify cross-domain duplication patterns
3. Conduct annual domain topology reassessment
page_texts.23:
[standards/governance/ai/STD-GOV-AI-005-ai-portfolio-hygiene.md#validation-criteria]

### Validation Criteria

| Validation Area | Criteria | Verification Method | Evidence Required |
| --------------- | --------- | ------------------- | -------------------- |
| Registry completeness | All 8 required fields present and current for every Proposed, Pilot, and Production capability | Registry audit | Capability registry |
| Overlap analysis at proposal | Every new capability proposal includes an overlap analysis before Pilot entry | Registry record review | Overlap analysis document |
| No unresolved high-overlap Production capabilities | All high-overlap Production capability pairs have a consolidation plan or architectural justification on record | Registry review | Consolidation plans or justification records |
| Rationalization trigger tracking | All capabilities meeting one or more rationalization trigger conditions are in active review | Monthly hygiene review log | Review meeting records |

---
page_texts.25:
[standards/governance/ai/STD-GOV-AI-005-ai-portfolio-hygiene.md#non-compliance-handling]

### Non-Compliance Handling

- Unregistered capability attempting to enter Pilot or Production: fail the governance gate; require registration before re-review
- Stale capability without owner or current registry data: move to Contained state pending remediation
- Persistent duplication without consolidation plan or justification: Enterprise Copilot Architecture Board intervention
page_texts.26:
[standards/governance/ai/STD-GOV-AI-005-ai-portfolio-hygiene.md#governance-oversight]

### Governance Oversight

- **Standards Owner**: Enterprise Copilot Architecture Board
- **Compliance Manager**: Platform Governance Team (monthly domain hygiene review; quarterly enterprise consolidation review)
- **Governance Body**: Enterprise Copilot Architecture Board (high-overlap exceptions; persistent duplication intervention)
